fluff.overview:
The Executioner-B, designated Gladiator-B by Inner Sphere forces, is a ninety-five-ton assault OmniMech introduced by Clan Burrock during the Golden Century. Produced under the auspices of ilKhan Zenos Danforth, who privately maneuvered to give Clan Burrock early access to OmniMech technology, the design was intended to restore the Burrock's assault-class combat capability after their tactics had shifted toward lighter hit-and-fade operations following Operation KLONDIKE. The resulting OmniMech eclipsed even Clan Coyote's Warlock in sheer payload capacity, establishing the Executioner-B as the premier heavy-assault OmniMech of its era.

Retroactively designated with the -B suffix after Clan Ghost Bear introduced the upgraded Executioner in 3001, the original design even so remained in widespread service across the Clan Homeworlds for well over a century after its debut. The Executioner-B's generous pod space ensured it retained relevance even as newer, more refined assault OmniMechs entered production, and its schematics ultimately served as the foundation for the Ghost Bear's faster successor.
fluff.capabilities:
The Executioner-B's most notable characteristic is its enormous forty-seven tons of pod space, nearly double that of its successor. This massive payload capacity allows the design to mount weapon loadouts rivaling dedicated assault BattleMechs, with configurations ranging from quad-PPC snipers to dual-Gauss rifle platforms. However, this impressive armament comes at a significant cost in mobility and reliability. The MechFusion 285 XL engine provides a top speed of only fifty-four kilometers per hour, well below average for Clan assault 'Mechs, and the chassis suffers from poor handling and sluggish responses that make it challenging to optimally engage faster opponents.

A pair of fixed Pryzhok WM 10 jump jets grant sixty meters of jump capability, enough to clear minor obstacles but insufficient for the tactical repositioning that defines more mobile OmniMechs. Fourteen tons of Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous armor actually exceeds the protection of the later Executioner, though the poor power distribution across the chassis means most configurations struggle with severe overheating. The sixteen standard double heat sinks prove woefully inadequate for the energy-hungry weapon loadouts the generous pod space invites, and nearly every configuration adds supplementary heat sinks that consume tonnage better spent on armament.
fluff.history:
The Executioner-B emerged during the mid-twenty-ninth century as Clan Burrock's bid to reclaim dominance in assault-class warfare. IlKhan Zenos Danforth, ostensibly a neutral arbiter of the OmniMech Trials, secretly facilitated Burrock's early access to the transformative technology, allowing them to field the Executioner-B before most rival Clans had completed their own OmniMech programs. The design's raw payload capacity made an immediate impression, and despite its practical shortcomings, the Executioner-B became a fixture in Burrock and Ghost Bear toumans alike, with most other Clans maintaining at least a few examples in their arsenals.

The design's greatest legacy proved to be its influence on the successor that would eventually bear its name. When Clan Ghost Bear acquired the Executioner-B's schematics through a Trial, their scientists recognized the platform's potential but identified the underpowered engine and unreliable power distribution as critical flaws. Rather than merely upgrading the existing design, the Ghost Bears replaced the MechFusion 285 XL with the far more powerful Heavy Force 380 XL and added a MASC system, fundamentally transforming the sluggish assault platform into one of the fastest 'Mechs in its weight class. The new Executioner entered production in 3001, and the original design was retroactively designated the Executioner-B to distinguish the two chassis.

Despite the introduction of its superior successor, the Executioner-B persisted in the Clan Homeworlds for over a century. During the Trial of Absorption against Clan Burrock in 3059, elements of Burrock's Omicron Galaxy employed Executioner-Bs in the desperate defense of Albion. Following the Absorption, Clan Star Adder enthusiastically incorporated the surviving Burrock Executioner-Bs into their touman, though their own Blood Asp program was nearing completion and reduced the urgency for an upgraded version of the aging design.

The Executioner-B saw rare but notable combat beyond the Homeworlds. In 3058, elements of Clan Ghost Bear's 304th Assault Cluster deployed a modified C configuration during an underwater assault on the planet Thun, where Ghost Bear forces sought raiders who had stolen the genetic legacies of the Clan's founders. The 'Mech's massive frame and heavy armament proved effective in the underwater environment of Jagger Bay, where the surrounding water actually improved heat sink performance and offset the chassis's notorious thermal problems. The engagement demonstrated that the Executioner-B, while outclassed in conventional engagements, could still find roles where its raw payload capacity compensated for its lack of speed.
fluff.deployment: The Prime configuration showcases the Executioner-B's philosophy of overwhelming firepower at the expense of heat management. Twin large pulse lasers provide accurate medium-range fire, while an extended-range PPC and Ultra Autocannon/20 deliver devastating damage at their respective optimal ranges. Twin Ultra AC/2s add long-range harassment capability. A single additional heat sink brings the total to seventeen, which remains far from adequate for the energy demands of this loadout. MechWarriors must exercise strict fire discipline, carefully cycling weapons to avoid the catastrophic heat spikes that plague this configuration during sustained engagements.
